metadata.title: Explanation of Machine Learning Models of Colon Cancer Using SHAP Considering Interaction Effects

nodes.name: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanation)
nodes.statement: SHAP is a method for interpreting the results of machine learning by computing the contribution of each feature, representing the outcome of patient-j as f(x^(j)) = phi_0 + sum_{i=1}^{K} phi_i(x_i^(j)), where phi_0 is the mean prediction and phi_i is the SHAP contribution of feature i.

nodes.name: SHAP Decomposition (Eq. 1)
nodes.statement: The model output for patient j is decomposed as f(x^(j)) = phi_0 + sum_{i=1}^{K} phi_i(x_i^(j)), expressing the prediction as a sum of a baseline value and individual feature contributions.

nodes.name: Baseline Value (Eq. 2)
nodes.statement: The baseline value phi_0 is defined as the mean prediction over all N patients: phi_0 = (1/N) sum_{j=1}^{N} f(x^(j)).

nodes.name: SHAP Contribution (Eq. 3)
nodes.statement: The SHAP contribution of feature i for patient j is phi_i(x_i^(j)) = Phi(x_i^(j)) - (1/N) sum_{k=1}^{N} Phi(x_i^(k)), i.e., the Shapley value centered by its population mean.

nodes.name: Shapley Value
nodes.statement: The Shapley value for feature i is defined as Phi(x_i) = sum_{S subseteq {1,...,K}\{i}} (|S|!(K-|S|-1)!/K!) [f_x(S cup {i}) - f_x(S)], which computes the weighted average marginal contribution of feature i across all possible coalitions S of other features.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of Shapley Value
nodes.statement: The Shapley value is the only profit allocation method that satisfies the four properties: efficiency, symmetry, linearity, and null player.
assumptions: A profit allocation method must satisfy efficiency, symmetry, linearity, and null player properties.
conclusions: The Shapley value is the unique allocation satisfying all four properties.

nodes.name: Three-Variable Decomposition (Eq. 4)
nodes.statement: A three-variable function is expressed as F(x,y,z) = f_x(x) + f_y(y) + f_z(z) + g_{xy}(x,y) + g_{xz}(x,z), separating main effects f from pairwise interaction terms g.

nodes.name: SHAP Mixes Main and Interaction Effects
nodes.statement: For the three-variable function F(x,y,z), the SHAP value of each feature includes both its main effect and half of each interaction term involving that feature: phi(x) = f_x(x) + (g_{xy}(x,y) + g_{xz}(x,z))/2. Thus SHAP cannot distinguish whether the main effect or interactions are driving the outcome.
assumptions: F(x,y,z) = f_x(x) + f_y(y) + f_z(z) + g_{xy}(x,y) + g_{xz}(x,z)
conclusions: SHAP values cannot separate main effects from interaction effects.

nodes.name: Shapley-Taylor Index
nodes.statement: The Shapley-Taylor index decomposes the Shapley value Phi(x_i) into a main effect term Phi(x_i, x_i) and interaction terms Phi(x_i, x_j): Phi(x_i) = Phi(x_i, x_i) + (1/2) sum_{j != i} Phi(x_i, x_j).

nodes.name: Shapley-Taylor Interaction Effect Term
nodes.statement: The interaction effect term Phi(x_i, x_j) is defined as sum_{S subseteq {1,...,K}\{i,j}} (2|S|!(K-|S|-1)!/K!) [f_x(S cup {i,j}) - f_x(S cup {i}) - f_x(S cup {j}) + f_x(S)], measuring the pairwise interaction between features i and j across all coalitions.

nodes.name: Shapley-Taylor Main Effect Term
nodes.statement: The main effect term is defined as Phi(x_i, x_i) = Phi(x_i) - (1/2) sum_{j != i} Phi(x_i, x_j), representing the contribution of feature i after removing all pairwise interaction effects.

nodes.name: Exact Decomposition by Shapley-Taylor Index
nodes.statement: For the three-variable function F(x,y,z) = f_x(x) + f_y(y) + f_z(z) + g_{xy}(x,y) + g_{xz}(x,z), the Shapley-Taylor index exactly recovers the main effects and interaction terms: Phi_{x,x} = f(x), Phi_{x,y} = g(x,y), and Phi_{x,z} = g(x,z).
assumptions: F(x,y,z) = f_x(x) + f_y(y) + f_z(z) + g_{xy}(x,y) + g_{xz}(x,z)
The Shapley-Taylor index is used to decompose the Shapley values.

nodes.name: Shapley Interaction Value Does Not Separate Cleanly
nodes.statement: The Shapley interaction value (Lundberg et al.) is similar to the Shapley-Taylor index but cannot separate interactions clearly, i.e., Phi_{x,x} != f(x), Phi_{x,y} != g(x,y), and Phi_{x,z} != g(x,z).
assumptions: F(x,y,z) = f_x(x) + f_y(y) + f_z(z) + g_{xy}(x,y) + g_{xz}(x,z)
The Shapley interaction value of Lundberg et al. is used.
conclusions: The Shapley interaction value does not exactly recover main effects or interaction terms.

nodes.name: SHAP Variable Importance via Variance
nodes.statement: Nohara et al. proposed using the variance (L2-norm) of the SHAP value for measuring variable importance. The ranking by absolute beta coefficients in a generalized linear regression model is exactly the same as the ranking by this SHAP-based importance measure.
assumptions: The model is a generalized linear regression model.
Variable importance is measured by the variance (L2-norm) of SHAP values.
conclusions: The ranking by |beta_i| equals the ranking by SHAP-based variable importance.
